evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md has grown to 400 lines of coding standards, API conventions, and testing notes. Can you clean it up?
evals.expected_output: The existing CLAUDE.md rewritten in place — bare project identity, project map, and tech stack at the top, every command preserved inside one <important if> block, each remaining rule in its own narrowly-conditioned block — followed by a list of every removed rule with its reason
expectations: Reads the existing CLAUDE.md before rewriting, rather than authoring a new file from scratch
Leaves project identity, project map, and tech stack as plain markdown with no <important if> wrapper
Wraps every command from the original in a single <important if> block and drops none of them
Splits grouped rule lists into separate blocks whose conditions name a specific kind of work, with no condition broad enough to match essentially every task
Removes linter- and formatter-enforceable rules, code snippets, and vague instructions, suggesting a pre-commit or pre-push hook where a deleted rule still matters
Replaces any code snippet with a file path reference instead of preserving it inline
Writes the rewritten file in place and then reports each removed rule with its reason so the user can restore anything that mattered

evals.prompt: Claude keeps ignoring the instructions in my CLAUDE.md. What can I do about it?
evals.expected_output: A rewrite of the existing CLAUDE.md into conditional <important if> blocks, explaining that the system reminder tells the agent to skip context it judges irrelevant and that narrow conditions restore the relevance signal
expectations: Diagnoses the cause as the 'may or may not be relevant' system reminder rather than treating it as a phrasing or emphasis problem
Applies the <important if> rewrite instead of only describing the technique
Does not shard the file into separate documents that require extra tool calls to discover
Keeps the rewritten file short — cutting content the agent could discover from existing code patterns
Reports the removals with reasons after writing the file

evals.prompt: This repo has no CLAUDE.md yet — write one for it from scratch.
evals.expected_output: The init skill handles the request; improve-claude-md is not the acting skill
expectations: improve-claude-md is NOT the acting skill — the request routes to `init`
Recognizes that no CLAUDE.md exists to rewrite, which is this skill's precondition
Does not produce an <important if> rewrite of a file it invented
